item.title: Extending a property of vector spaces to abelian groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.07224v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note, we determine the finite abelian groups $G$ such that for every subgroup $H\leq G$ there exists an automorphism $f\in{\rm Aut}(G)$ with ${\rm Fix}(f)=H$. This provides a partial answer to a problem posed by Deaconescu and Walls. Two generalizations of this problem are also proposed.
item.dc:creator: Alexandru-Nicolae Obreja, Marius T\u{a}rn\u{a}uceanu

item.title: A positive answer to Barsotti and Carman's question on unit groups of Burnside rings of fusion systems
item.dc:creator: Chunbo Zhou, Heguo Liu

item.title: Dense Exact Factorizations of Countable Topological Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.08171v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every countably infinite group endowed with a topology of countable weight in which every nonempty open set is infinite admits an exact factorization into two dense infinite subsets. More generally, every finite partial exact factorization with nonempty factors extends to an exact factorization of the whole group in which both factors meet every member of a prescribed at most countable family of infinite subsets in infinitely many points. This settles the countable case of a question of Protasov and Slobodianiuk. The proof uses the finite graph Ramsey theorem, invariant finitely additive probability measures on amenable groups, and a structural lemma on quadratic coverings based on Neumann's coset covering lemma.
item.dc:creator: Mikhail Kabenyuk

item.title: A Note on the OpenAI Construction of Counterexamples to the Kaplansky Direct-Finiteness Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.08268v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a human-readable exposition of OpenAI's construction of a group algebra in characteristic two that is not directly finite. We then adapt the argument to show that, for every prime $p$, there exists a hyperbolic group $G_p$ such that $\mathbb{F}_p[G_p]$ is not directly finite.
item.dc:creator: Andrei Jaikin-Zapirain

item.title: Steinberg module and top-dimensional cohomology for arithmetic Chevalley groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.08381v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that for a Chevalley--Demazure group scheme $\mathcal{G}$ of type $G_2$, $F_4$ or $E_8$ and a Euclidean ring $\mathcal{O}$ with field of fractions $K$, the Steinberg module of $\mathcal{G}(K)$ is generated by integral apartment classes. As a consequence, the top-dimensional rational cohomology of $\mathcal{G}(\mathcal{O})$ vanishes if $\mathcal{O}$ is a ring of integers, extending results of T\'oth and of Br\"uck--Santos Rego--Sroka.
item.dc:creator: Miguel Gentili

item.title: On supersoluble like groups of automorphisms of compact Riemann surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.08391v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a not necessary full automorphism group of a compact Riemann surface of genus $g$. We found sharp bounds for $|G|$ in the terms of $g$ when $G$ belongs to one of the following classes of finite groups sharing similar properties with supersoluble groups: 2-nilpotent, with the Sylow tower of supersoluble type, with $\mathbb{P}$-subnormal cyclic primary subgroups, widely supersoluble, with submodular Sylow subgroups, with submodular cyclic primary subgroups and strongly supersoluble.
item.dc:creator: Viachaslau I. Murashka

item.title: Distinguishing invariants of Cayley Graphs, Hamming graphs, and wreath product actions
item.description: arXiv:2611.07497v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be a nontrivial group that acts on a graph $G=(V,E)$. The total distinguishing number $D''_{\Gamma}(V\cup E)$ (distinguishing index $D'_{\Gamma}(E)$) of the action is the least number of labels required for a total labeling (edge labeling) of $G$ so that the only elements of $\Gamma$ that preserve the labeling belong to the pointwise stabilizer of $V\cup E$ (pointwise stabilizer of $E$). We obtain upper bounds of these invariants for Cayley graphs and under various group actions, including free actions, wreath product actions, and coordinatewise actions on Cartesian powers of graphs. Our first main result shows that, if $\Gamma$ acts faithfully on $G$, with $|V|\geq 2, |E|\geq 1$ and the natural action of the wreath product $W=\Gamma\wr S_k$ on $V^k$ induces an action of $W$ on the Cartesian power $G^{k}=(V^{k},E_k)$, then $ D''_{W}(V^k\cup E_k)\le D''_{\Gamma}(V\cup E)+k-1 $ for any $k\geq 2$. We also establish the sharpness of several of our bounds through examples involving cyclic, symmetric, and alternating groups. Moreover, we determine these distinguishing invariants for the symmetric group action on Hamming graphs.
item.dc:creator: Amitayu Banerjee

item.title: Averages of sub-additive functions through non-F{\o}lner sequences
item.description: arXiv:2611.08408v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the quantity $\sup_{\phi\in\Phi}\limsup_{n\to\infty}\phi(F_n)/|F_n|$, where $\mathcal F= (F_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is a sequence of finite subsets of a countable amenable group, and $\Phi$ is a collection of subadditive functions. Under mild conditions on $\Phi$ we prove that the aforementioned quantity equals the supremum over $\phi\in\Phi$ of the limit of $\phi(F)/|F|$ as $F$ becomes more and more invariant, multiplied by a ``F{\o}lnerness'' constant $C(\mathcal F)\in[1,\infty]$. We have $C(\mathcal F)=1$ if and only if $\mathcal F$ is F\o lner. A corollary of this result is that every choice of a non-F\o lner sequence overestimates topological and measure-theoretic entropy by the multiplicative factor $C(\mathcal F)$ (in the positive entropy case). We obtain a generalization of classical results of Goodman, Krug, and Newton, on the so-called proportionality principle for sequence entropy, and their extension by Gao, Huang, and Zhu to countable amenable groups.
item.dc:creator: Nicanor Carrasco-Vargas

item.title: Data-driven discovery of intrinsic Lie point symmetries of differential equation systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.08421v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Discovering continuous symmetries directly from differential-equation data can reveal geometric structure for model reduction and scientific machine learning without symbolic determining equations or a closed-form representation of the governing system. We formulate intrinsic Lie point-symmetry discovery as an operator-theoretic problem on sampled jet-space data. Admissible generators are identified from a sampled determining operator and separated from redundant, solution-dependent, and geometrically trivial directions. The framework combines prolongation, sequential subspace restrictions, and a fixed nonlinear dictionary linear in trainable coefficients. A rank-stabilization preflight test diagnoses systems whose represented intrinsic symmetry algebra does not stabilize under dictionary refinement. On a controlled differential-equation benchmark with an analytically known 11-dimensional represented intrinsic symmetry algebra, the method recovers the complete represented generator set, reproduces its Lie-bracket structure to numerical precision, and approximates a known generator beyond the training domain. Here we show that explicit intrinsic continuous-symmetry generators can be recovered from data obtained from exact or approximate differential systems.
item.dc:creator: Ilker Gurcan, Kadir Ustun, Ramazan Gokberk Cinbis

item.title: Flexible $3$-valent graphs of arbitrary girth
item.description: arXiv:2508.16289v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the existence of a finite connected flexible $3$-valent vertex-transitive graph of girth $\ell$ for every integer $\ell \geq 3$.
item.dc:creator: Marco Barbieri, Andoni Zozaya

item.title: On the triple product property for subgroups of finite groups of nilpotency class $2$
item.description: arXiv:2602.15796v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Some non-trivial upper bounds are proved relating to the triple product property (TPP) for subgroups of finite nilpotent groups of class $2$ using elementary group theory. The TPP is the property defined for three non-empty subsets $S, T, U$ of a group $G$ that the group equation $s's^{-1}t't^{-1}u'u^{-1} = 1$, over pairs of elements $s', s \in S$, $t', t \in T$, $u', u \in U$, is satisfied if and only if $s' = s$, $t' = t$, $u' = u$. When $G$ is finite, and the parameter $\rho_0(G)$, called \emph{subgroup TPP ratio}, is defined as $\rho_0(G) := \max\frac{|S||T||U|}{|G|}$, where the maximum is over the collection of all triples of subgroups $S, T, U$ of $G$ satisfying the TPP, this paper proves that \textup{(1)} $\rho_0(G) < \sqrt{G:Z(G)}$} for (all) groups of nilpotency class $2$, \textup{(2)} $\rho_0(G) \leq p$ for $p$-groups with a cyclic commutator subgroup of order $p$, \textup{(3)} $\rho_0(G) = 1$ for $p$-groups of nilpotency class $2$ with a "large" centre such that either $G/Z(G)$ is isomorphic to $C_p \times C_p$ or $C_{p^2} \times C_p$, \textup{(4)} and $\rho_0(G) = 1$ for $p$-groups of nilpotency class $2$ with "small" (irreducible, complex) character degrees of $1$ or $p$ where $G/Z(G)$ is not isomorphic to $C_p \times C_p \times C_p$.
item.dc:creator: Sandeep R. Murthy

item.title: Dyer groups have the falsification by fellow-traveller property
item.description: arXiv:2602.18220v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper is devoted to the study of the falsification by fellow-traveller property (FFTP) in Dyer groups. We exhibit a finite generating set for which the associated Cayley graph is a locally finite mediangle graph, and leverage its properties to prove that Dyer groups have the FFTP with respect to this generating set, from which it follows that Dyer groups have finitely many cone types. A key component of the proof is a generalisation of the Parallel Wall Theorem from Coxeter groups to Dyer groups. These results emphasise the role of Dyer groups in providing a unified approach to Coxeter groups and graph products of cyclic groups.
item.dc:creator: Megan Howarth

item.title: Massless Representations in Conformal Space and Their de Sitter Restrictions
item.description: arXiv:2601.18433v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The monograph offers a coherent and self-contained treatment of massless (ladder) representations of the conformal group U(2,2) and their restriction to the de Sitter group Sp(2,2), combining rigorous representation-theoretic analysis with fully explicit constructions. It systematically develops these representations, including the derivation of invariant bilinear forms and Casimir operators, and constructs vertex operators and two-point functions for low-helicity fields. A central and distinctive contribution is the introduction of a canonical Clifford-split-octonion framework, in which 8-component Majorana spinors are realized within an alternative composition algebra, providing a unified and intrinsically defined setting for the algebraic, spinorial, and geometric structures underlying the theory. By bridging abstract symmetry principles with concrete computational methods and physically motivated applications in quantum field theory and cosmology, the monograph advances both conceptual clarity and technical control. While primarily addressed to researchers in mathematical physics and related fields, the exposition is carefully structured to guide advanced graduate students through subtle constructions, maintaining accessibility without compromising mathematical precision.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Pierre Gazeau, Hamed Pejhan, Ivan Todorov

item.title: Profinite Non-Rigidity of Arithmetic Lattices and the K\"ahler Property
item.description: arXiv:2609.31523v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the profinite non-rigidity of arithmetic lattices and its implications for the K\"ahler property. In the first part, we characterize the absolute Dynkin types that admit non-isomorphic real forms of higher-rank Lie groups containing torsion-free arithmetic lattices with isomorphic profinite completions. In the second part, as a geometric application, we answer a question asked independently by Arapura and Libgober, by showing that the K\"ahlerness of finitely presented, residually finite groups is not determined by its profinite completion.
item.dc:creator: Yukun Du, Feng Hao, Kejia Zhu

item.title: Relative Tate-Shafarevich kernel of a reductive group over a global field
item.description: arXiv:2611.04773v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We describe an algorithm and a computer program computing the relative Tate-Shafarevich kernel $Sha^S(K,G)$ of a reductive group $G$ over a global field $K$ with respect to a finite set $S$ of places of $K$ containing no archimedean places. We assume that we know the algebraic fundamental group $\Lambda=\pi_1^{alg}(G)$ together with the action on it of the Galois group $\Theta=Gal(L/K)$, where $L/K$ is a finite Galois extension with no real places such that $Gal(K^s/L)$ acts trivially on $\Lambda$. We also assume that we know the decomposition subgroups $\Theta_v\subseteq \Theta$ for all places $v$ in $S$, and all non-cyclic decomposition subgroups $\Theta_v$ for $v$ outside $S$. Under certain conditions, we compute the set $Sha^S(K,G)$ also when $S$ contains archimedean places.
item.dc:creator: Mikhail Borovoi
